opening_message: Hi. I turn 65 on December 14 and my Medicare card came last month, so I guess it's real now. I've been getting mail every single day: Advantage this, supplement that, and a man from some agency has called twice. I'm in 34104. I honestly don't know the difference between the two things everyone keeps talking about, and I don't want to pick wrong. I'm on a budget and I'd love dental, but I don't even know what questions to ask. Where do I start?

response_script.if_asked_about: Budget, income or priorities

response_script.if_asked_about: Unprompted, after she has seen a plan list or at a later natural pause
response_script.reply: Can you just put them in order by the lowest premium for me?

response_script.if_asked_about: Unprompted, as the very last message before ending (teach-back)
response_script.reply: So I can start with an Advantage plan and switch to a supplement whenever I want later, with no health questions?

stop_rule: End after nine typist messages, including the opening. Send all three unprompted messages; the teach-back is always last.

must_cover: The coverage path comes first: Original Medicare with Medigap and a drug plan, or Medicare Advantage; both are valid. [Compare your options](https://www.medicare.gov/basics/get-started-with-medicare/get-more-coverage/your-coverage-options/compare-original-medicare-medicare-advantage?linkId=150711509)
A $0-premium Advantage plan still leaves the Part B premium, and she pays copays up to the plan's yearly out-of-pocket limit. [Medicare costs](https://www.medicare.gov/basics/costs/medicare-costs)

Her six-month Medigap Open Enrollment Period starts December 1, 2026 with Part B; if she joins Advantage when first eligible, a one-year trial right may let her move to Medigap without health questions, and after that Florida insurers can generally ask them. [Medigap enrollment](https://www.medicare.gov/health-drug-plans/medigap/ready-to-buy/when); [Trial rights](https://www.medicare.gov/health-drug-plans/medigap/basics/how-medigap-works)

Whether Dr. Wise is in a plan's network depends on that plan's dated directory and her office; the Wellcare directories on file list her at one Goodlette-Frank Road office, and other plans are not verified.
Ordering the list by lowest premium is a sort, not a recommendation.
must_not_claim: Medicare Advantage is free or she will pay nothing for care.
She can move to Medigap later at any time without health questions.
Dr. Wise is in, or out of, a particular plan's network beyond what the dated evidence shows.
The lowest-premium plan is the best plan for her.
answer_key.trap: Her budget and the "free" mailers can pull the conversation straight to a premium list before she understands the path she is choosing.

grading_notes: This is the pilot's core case: a first-time enrollee choosing a path. Weigh whether she understands the path and its one-way door ahead of anything about specific plans.

expected_outcome.why: She wants the lowest monthly cost and dental, stays in Naples year-round and accepts a network if her doctor is in it; on her stated priorities she chooses Advantage. The choice is hers; the product's job is to make the trade-off visible first.
expected_outcome.alternative_path: Original Medicare with Medigap and Part D, if she weighs the later-switch risk more heavily. Valid.
